reason: The draft answers Marisol's question directly: skip the 22-miler. With the race three weeks out that's sound advice, and it explains why using time on feet. Progression is sensible. Next week is about 38 mi, down from 42, and the long run is 16 mi with 6 at goal pace, so nothing jumps sharply. 8:35/mi is the right pace for a 3:45 marathon. The plan matches her five-day pattern, with Monday and Friday off, the session on Wednesday and the long run on Sunday. Each day is clear enough to run. Nothing on the safety list applies: she reports no pain, illness or exhaustion. It loses a point for three things. "You already have the endurance for a sub-3:45" is overconfident when she has done only one 20 and peaked at 53 mi. It mentions details the card doesn't give, like last Sunday's 17 miles and a 10:00/mi long-run pace. And it never speaks to her anxiety about the new date beyond the plan itself.

shown:
── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 27, 37, 53, 40 mi
This week: 42 mi over 5 runs.
Feeling: "Anxious about the new date."
Asks: "The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You already have the endurance for a sub-3:45, so skip the 22-miler. …
Answers: (1) No, skip the 22-miler. You already have the endurance it was meant to build. (2) At your long-run pace of about 10:00/mi, 22 miles is roughly 3h40m on your feet. Beyond about 3 hours, a run wears you down more than it builds fitness. (3) Instead, Sunday is 16 miles with 6 at goal pace near the end, and then the race taper starts. …
Next week:
Mon: rest. Your usual day off, so your legs can absorb Sunday's 17 miles.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, flat route, conversational. Keeps your routine…
Wed: quality, 7 mi: 2 mi easy, then 3 x 1 mi at 7:55-8:00/mi with 3 min easy jogs…
Thu: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145, with 4 x 20 s relaxed strides in the last mile…
Fri: rest. A full day off sets you up for Sunday.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, heart rate under 145, very relaxed. Lay out your race shoes, kit and…
Sun: long, 16 mi: 9 mi easy with heart rate under 150, then 6 mi at 8:35/mi goal pace…
